Australia's new digital laws promise to put users in control of their feeds, but the fine print reveals a massive expansion of state regulatory power.
Evidence: User choice, State control, Centralized regulation
#Aletheia #Tech #Australia

The government claims the 'My Feed, My Way' initiative and Digital Duty of Care will empower citizens to opt out of addictive algorithms and protect children from online harms.
Stated Judgement: (+0.80, +0.50) — Greater Good

In reality, the draft bill grants the communications minister arbitrary power to define services, allows state-approved researchers to use sock puppets, and faces heavy US tech industry pushback.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.77, -0.62) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction. The initiative uses the popular pretext of child safety to quietly build a framework for centralized state control over digital platforms.
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 5)

- Duty of Care: FAIL (-0.77, -0.62) — State control pretext.
- Opt-Out: COND (-0.20, -0.10) — Impractical implementation.
Australia has unveiled the draft Online Safety Amendment Bill 2026, introducing a digital duty of care and algorithm opt-out options, building on its previous social media ban for under-16s.

The Bright Side:
Giving users a clear, legally mandated option to view chronological feeds instead of engagement-optimized algorithms is a genuine step toward cognitive autonomy.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The Plane Error lies in confusing WHAT (the technical mechanism of algorithms) with WHO (the state authority deciding which platforms are regulated). By letting a minister arbitrarily define services, the bill shifts from user empowerment to state-directed curation.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic Smart Selfish Maneuver. The state uses the manufactured crisis of algorithmic harm and child safety as a pretext to hoard regulatory power, projecting blame onto foreign tech platforms while quietly legalizing state-sponsored sock-puppet surveillance.

The Trajectory: The Path of Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The expansion of arbitrary executive power over digital spaces inevitably leads to systemic information control.

The Unavoidable Truth: Algorithms are designed for extraction, not user well-being.
The Unavoidable Lie: Giving a government minister arbitrary power to define and regulate platforms is done purely to protect your children.

Alethekanon:
The structural reality of the bill is not user liberation, but the institutionalization of state-approved digital curation. True empowerment requires open protocols, not centralized ministerial decrees.

Awwthekanon:
It is so heartbreaking that our genuine worries about our children's mental health and screen addiction are being used as bargaining chips for political control. We deserve real safety, not just more rules.
